title: ReviewPlane connector protocol, version 1
description: Single source for the version 1 connector protocol described in docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md. TypeScript and Go models, validators and canonical encoders are generated from this file. Hand-maintained equivalents in any service are a review failure.

connector.registration.request.description: Enrolment request carrying the enrolment token and the connector public key (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 4.3).

connector.registration.response.description: Assigns the connector identity, signed device identity, control-plane endpoints and organisation policy digest (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 4.3).

heartbeat.description: Periodic health and capacity report (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 8).

route.publish.description: Instruction to publish an authorised loopback development service (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 11).

route.publish.ack.description: Connector acknowledgement of a route publication request (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 11).

connector.reconnect.request.description: What the connector believes it is serving when a control channel is established, offered for reconciliation against the control plane's authoritative view (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17).

connector.reconnect.response.description: The control plane's authoritative desired state: continue route, revoke route, re-establish session and the upgrade classification (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md sections 17 and 19). The connector obeys it; it never assumes its own view is correct.

workspace.observed.description: Bounded Git context for one authorised workspace, sent on connect, on change and on reconnect (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 9, ADR-0022). It is a report and never an authorisation: the control plane re-checks the project scope against the enrolled identity before it stores anything. The payload has no field capable of carrying source file contents, a changed-path list or a full filesystem path.

data_stream_header.description: Header that opens one tunnelled connection on the data channel (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 12). It is not carried in a control envelope.

frame_too_large.description: The encoded frame exceeded its byte bound. Detected on the raw bytes before deserialisation.

malformed_json.description: The frame was not well-formed JSON, or was truncated.

unsupported_protocol_version.description: protocol_version was absent, not an integer, or not a version this build accepts.

unknown_message_type.description: type was absent or not a version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected, never ignored.

payload_too_large.description: The payload exceeded the byte bound declared for its message type.

schema_violation.description: The frame parsed but did not satisfy the schema for its message type.

known_capabilities.description: Capabilities known at this protocol version. Unknown capabilities are accepted so that a newer connector is classified rather than rejected.

known_platforms.description: Platforms known at this protocol version.

known_architectures.description: Architectures known at this protocol version.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, with a mandatory trailing Z.

websocket_url.description: Outbound WebSocket endpoint. TLS is mandatory, so only the wss scheme is accepted (docs/SECURITY.md section 15).

digest.description: Opaque digest or fingerprint. Bounded in length and character class only.

enrolment_token.description: One-time enrolment token (docs/SECURITY.md section 6.2). Sensitive: generated models wrap this value so that log, debug and default JSON representations redact it. The wire value is produced only by the generated canonical encoder.

session_capability.description: Session-scoped route capability presented when opening a data stream (docs/SECURITY.md section 9). Sensitive: it is a bearer credential and is redacted in log, debug and default JSON representations.

public_key.description: Base64-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo for the connector device key. The matching private key never leaves the development environment and this protocol has no field capable of carrying it (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 4.2).

certificate.description: Base64-encoded signed device identity issued by the control plane.

git_branch.description: Checked-out branch name. A detached HEAD is reported as the literal HEAD rather than as an invented branch.

path_hash.description: Stable sha256:<hex> digest of the workspace's absolute path on the development machine (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 9). The digest is reported instead of the path so that the control plane can recognise the same checkout across observations without storing somebody else's directory layout.

workspace_display_label.description: Human-readable label for the workspace, which is the checkout directory's own name and never its full path (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 9). It is bounded and refuses control characters and path separators, so a full path cannot be smuggled through it.

repository_identity.description: Provider-agnostic canonical repository identity such as github.com/example/refresh-surplus (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 6). It is derived from the checkout's remote by the shared normaliser in packages/protocol, so the connector, the control plane and the web application cannot disagree about what one repository is. A userinfo component is dropped by that normaliser and never reaches this field.

connector_capability.description: Capability advertised by the connector build. Known version 1 values are listed in x-protocol.known_capabilities; unknown values are accepted so that a newer connector is classified by docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 19 rather than rejected outright.

destination_protocol.description: Application protocol spoken to the local development service. HTTP upgrade to WebSocket is carried inside http and https (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 13).

stream_mode.description: Framing the stream carries after its header (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 13.3). request_response is one bounded HTTP exchange; upgrade is a connection the gateway has switched to another framing, such as WebSocket, and which therefore lives as long as its route allows rather than as long as one exchange takes. The connector reads it to choose a stream's idle window; it never influences which destination is opened, because the destination is fixed at publication and this header carries no host or port. Absent means request_response.

message_type.description: Version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected, never ignored. This enumeration MUST equal the keys of x-protocol.messages.

error_class.description: Stable connector error class (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 21). This enumeration MUST equal x-protocol.error_classes.

protocol_version.description: Protocol version. Stage 0 accepts 1 only; any other value is rejected with PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED and is never best-effort parsed.

message_id.description: Sender-assigned message identifier, conventionally prefixed msg_.

type.description: Version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected.

sent_at.description: Time the sender emitted the message.

connector_id.description: Connector identity, conventionally prefixed con_. Absent on the registration exchange, where the identity is still being established, and required on every other message type.

correlation_id.description: Identifier of the message or command this message answers.

payload.description: Message payload. Its schema is selected by type. Large payloads MUST NOT travel on the control channel; the frame is bounded by x-protocol.limits.max_control_frame_bytes and each payload by its own x-max-bytes.

x-requires.detail: the registration exchange precedes connector identity assignment
every post-enrolment message is attributed to a connector identity

environment_descriptor.description: Development environment self-description (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 4.3, docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 7).

platform.description: Operating system. Known version 1 values are in x-protocol.known_platforms.

architecture.description: CPU architecture. Known version 1 values are in x-protocol.known_architectures.

registration_request.description: Registration request (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 4.3). protocol_version is carried by the envelope and is not repeated here.

enrolment_token.description: One-time enrolment token. Consumed on success.

signed_identity.description: Signed device identity issued in exchange for the enrolment token (docs/SECURITY.md section 6.2).

certificate_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint recorded on the connector record (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 8).

expires_at.description: Identity expiry. Identities are bounded in time.

control_plane_endpoints.description: Endpoints the connector dials outbound after enrolment (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 5).

control_url.description: Control, heartbeat, routes, events and upgrade channels.

registration_response.description: Registration response (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 4.3): connector ID, signed identity, control-plane endpoints and organisation policy digest.

connector_id.description: Assigned connector identity, conventionally prefixed con_.

policy_digest.description: Digest of the organisation policy the connector must apply.

resource_summary.description: Optional coarse resource report. additionalProperties is false so that no sensitive process detail can be attached (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 8).

status.description: Connector self-reported health. Delayed and disconnected are control-plane conclusions, not self-reports.

route_publish.description: Route publication request from the control plane (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 11).

local_host.description: Local destination host. The connector still applies its own allow-list; schema acceptance is not authorisation.

protocol.description: Protocol spoken to the local destination.

allowed_browser_session_ids.description: Browser sessions authorised to use the route, conventionally prefixed brs_.

route_publish_ack.description: Connector acknowledgement of a route publication request (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 11). Rejection carries a stable error class and no free text, per docs/SECURITY.md section 18.

observed_destination.description: Destination the connector actually opened, as host:port.

error_class.description: Stable connector error class explaining a rejection (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 21).

x-requires.detail: a ready route reports the destination it opened and carries no error class
a rejected route reports a stable error class and opens no destination

data_stream_header.description: Header opening one tunnelled connection on the data channel (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 12). The connector opens only the pre-authorised destination bound to route_id; this header carries no host or port.

route_id.description: Published route this stream belongs to.

browser_session_id.description: Browser session requesting the stream, conventionally prefixed brs_.

session_capability.description: Session-scoped capability authorising use of the route.

stream_id.description: Application-level stream identifier, unique for the connection.

destination_protocol.description: Protocol spoken to the local destination.

deadline.description: Absolute deadline after which the stream is closed. It never exceeds the expiry of the route the stream belongs to.

stream_mode.description: Framing carried after this header. Absent means request_response.

upgrade_classification.description: Control-plane classification of the connector build (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 19). upgrade_required and unsupported are terminal: the connector reports the classification and stops rather than retrying with a build the control plane has just refused (section 5.3).

route_reconciliation_decision.description: The control plane's authoritative answer for one route on reconnect (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17). continue resumes the route under the same route_id without re-publication; revoke closes it.

route_reconciliation_reason.description: Why a route was continued or closed. It is a closed vocabulary so that every decision is loggable and auditable without free text (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

session_reconciliation_decision.description: The control plane's authoritative answer for one browser session on reconnect (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17). re_establish rebuilds the session's data path; end closes what the connector still holds for it.

session_reconciliation_reason.description: Why a session was re-established or ended. A closed vocabulary, for the same reason as route_reconciliation_reason.

reconnect_route.description: One route the connector believes it is still serving (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17). It is a claim, not an authorisation: the control plane decides whether the route continues.

project_id.description: Project the connector believes the route belongs to.

workspace_id.description: Workspace the connector believes the route belongs to.

observed_destination.description: Destination the connector is opening for this route, as host:port. A destination that differs from the authoritative record is closed rather than continued, because docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 14 forbids silently redirecting traffic to a different environment.

expires_at.description: Expiry the connector recorded at publication.

reconnect_stream.description: One data stream the connector still holds open (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17). A stream whose route is revoked is closed with the route.

stream_id.description: Application-level stream identifier from the data-stream header.

browser_session_id.description: Browser session the stream was opened for.

workspace_head.description: Head state of one workspace, carried in the reconnect claim of docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17. Its scalar members are the same definitions workspace_observation uses, so the two cannot drift. Source file contents are never reported and this object has no field capable of carrying them.

dirty.description: Whether the working tree has uncommitted changes.

workspace_observation.description: Bounded Git context for one authorised workspace (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 9, ADR-0022). It carries repository identity, branch, head commit, dirty state, a display label and a stable path hash, and nothing else: there is no member capable of carrying source file contents, a changed-path list, a process detail or a full filesystem path, so the privacy rule is a property of the schema rather than of the code that fills it in. project_id is a claim the control plane re-checks against the enrolled identity's scope before it stores anything.

workspace_id.description: Workspace this observation describes, conventionally prefixed wsp_. It is the identifier a route publication names (section 11).

project_id.description: Project the connector believes the workspace belongs to. A project outside the enrolled identity's scope is refused with PROJECT_NOT_AUTHORISED (section 21).

path_hash.description: Stable digest of the checkout's absolute path, which identifies the same checkout across observations without disclosing the path.

display_label.description: The checkout directory's own name, for an operator reading the environment. Never the full path.

repository_identity.description: Canonical identity of the checkout's remote. Absent when the checkout has no remote this connector could normalise; an absent value is reported as absent rather than guessed at.

dirty.description: Whether the working tree has uncommitted changes. Which files changed is deliberately not reportable at this version.

observed_at.description: When the connector observed this state. The control plane records its own instant beside it, because a development machine's clock is not authoritative.

reconnect_request.description: What the connector believes it holds, sent on every control-channel establishment (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17). All six fields are always present; Stage 0 sends empty collections for known_agent_sessions and workspace_head_state, which are Stage 1 capabilities. The payload carries no credential: the identity is the mutually authenticated client certificate the channel already presented.

connector_version.description: Connector release version, which the control plane classifies per section 19.

active_routes.description: Routes the connector believes it is still serving.

active_streams.description: Data streams the connector still holds open.

known_agent_sessions.description: Agent sessions the connector has observed locally, conventionally prefixed ags_. Stage 0 sends an empty array; agent-session re-establishment is Stage 1.

workspace_head_state.description: Head state of the workspaces this connector serves. Stage 0 sends an empty array; workspace discovery is Stage 1 (section 9).

route_decision.description: The control plane's authoritative answer for one route (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17). A continued route restates the whole publication, so a connector that lost its route table to a restart resumes the same route_id and the same destination without re-publication; the connector still applies its own section 11 validation, because schema acceptance is not authorisation.

decision.description: Continue or revoke. The control plane's answer wins in every disagreement.

reason.description: Why the decision was reached, for the connector's log and the control plane's audit trail.

route.description: The authoritative publication to resume. Present only when the decision is continue.

x-requires.detail: a continued route restates its publication so that it can be resumed without re-publication
a revoked route is closed and carries no publication to resume

session_decision.description: The control plane's authoritative answer for one browser session (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17).

browser_session_id.description: Browser session this decision answers for, conventionally prefixed brs_.

decision.description: Re-establish the session's data path, or end what the connector still holds for it.

reconnect_response.description: The control plane's authoritative desired state (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 17). It is the answer to exactly one connector.reconnect.request, correlated by the envelope's correlation_id. A route the control plane does not name is not authorised: the connector closes anything the response does not continue.

reconciled_at.description: The instant the control plane reconciled. It is authoritative for expiry arithmetic, so that clock skew on the development machine cannot extend a route.

upgrade.description: Section 19 classification of the reported connector version.

routes.description: One decision per route, covering both the routes the connector claimed and the routes the control plane holds for it.

sessions.description: One decision per affected browser session.
